source: GAA Official Guide Part 2, Playing Rules of Hurling (edition effective 10 March 2025)
note: Paraphrased summaries written for this prototype, not the official wording. Check every rule against the Official Guide before relying on it.

rules.title: Ball in play
rules.text: The ball is in play from the throw-in or a puck until play is stopped, the ball crosses or hits a boundary flag, or it touches someone who is not a player.

rules.title: Striking the ball
rules.text: A player may strike the ball with the hurley on the ground, in the air, after dropping it from the hand, or after lifting it with the hurley.

rules.title: Running with the ball on the hurley
rules.text: A player may run while balancing the ball on the hurley or hopping it on the hurley. There is no step limit while the ball is on the hurley.

rules.title: Catching and taking into the hand
rules.text: A player may catch the ball, play it on the hurley and bring it back into the hand once. A player who has not caught the ball may bring it from the hurley to the hand twice.

rules.title: Hand and foot
rules.text: The ball may be struck with the hand, kicked, or flicked up off the ground with the foot.

rules.title: Hand on the ground
rules.text: A player may not touch the ball with the hand while it is on the ground, unless the player has fallen or been knocked down and the ball in their hand touches the ground.

rules.title: Carrying, steps and the handpass
rules.text: A player may carry the ball in the hand for no more than four steps, or hold it for no longer than it takes to take four steps. The ball may be released from the hand and struck with a definite striking action of the hand, which is how a legal handpass is made.

rules.title: Tackling
rules.text: A player may tackle an opponent to win the ball.

rules.title: Shoulder charge
rules.text: A fair shoulder-to-shoulder charge is allowed with at least one foot on the ground, on an opponent who has the ball, is playing the ball, or is moving towards the ball with you. The goalkeeper may not be charged inside the small rectangle.

rules.title: Run-up outside the field
rules.text: A player taking a free puck, sideline puck or puck-out may go outside the field for a run-up. Otherwise players must stay inside the field of play.

rules.title: Intercepting a free
rules.text: A defending player may raise the hurley or hands to block or intercept a free puck.

rules.title: Throw-in
rules.text: The game starts and restarts after half-time with the referee throwing the ball in between two players from each team at the halfway line. All other players stay behind their own 45m lines.

rules.title: Where a free is taken
rules.text: After a foul, play restarts with a free puck where the foul happened, with exceptions. A defender's aggressive foul inside the large rectangle gives a penalty puck; a technical foul there gives a free from the centre of the 20m line. A defender's foul outside the large rectangle but inside the 20m line gives a free on the 20m line opposite where it happened.

rules.title: Fouls at the same time
rules.text: If players from both teams foul at the same time, play restarts with a throw-in.

rules.title: Distances and the penalty puck
rules.text: Opponents must be at least 20m from a free puck and 13m from a throw-in. A penalty puck is struck from the centre of the 20m line, or from the arc after the taker brings the ball back to seven metres. Defenders must take their set positions, and the referee may order a retake if a defender moves or fouls first.

rules.title: Taking a free puck
rules.text: The taker may lift the ball with the hurley and strike it, or strike it on the ground. If the lift fails, the taker must strike the ball on the ground straight away.

rules.title: Puck-out
rules.text: A puck-out is taken from inside the small rectangle. The goalkeeper may take the ball into the hand. Opponents must stay outside the 20m line until the ball is struck, and the ball must travel 13m before another player from the defending team plays it.

rules.title: 65m free (a '65')
rules.text: If a defender plays the ball over their own endline wide of the posts, the attacking team gets a free puck on the 65m line opposite where the ball went out.

rules.title: Sideline puck (sideline cut)
rules.text: When the ball goes over the sideline, the other team gets a free puck from the ground where it crossed. If the referee cannot tell who played it last, there is a throw-in 13m in from the sideline. A ball hitting a corner or side flag counts as having gone out.

rules.title: Stoppage for serious injury
rules.text: If play is stopped for a serious injury, it restarts with a free puck to the team in possession where play stopped, or from the 20m line if that was inside the opponents' 20m line. A score cannot be made directly from this free. If no team had possession, there is a throw-in.

rules.title: Ball touches a non-player
rules.text: If the ball touches someone who is not a player, there is a throw-in at that spot. If it happened during a free puck, the free is retaken.

rules.title: Goals and points
rules.text: A goal is scored when the ball goes over the goal-line under the crossbar and is worth three points. A point is scored when the ball goes over the crossbar and is worth one point. An attacking player holding the ball may not carry it over the goal-line or throw or hand it into the goal.

rules.title: Scoring with the hand
rules.text: A point or goal may be scored by striking the ball with the hand while it is in the air, except that an attacker in possession may not score a goal with the hand.

rules.title: Deflections, posts and interference
rules.text: If a non-player or the referee stops the ball crossing, the score can still be given. If a post or crossbar is knocked out of place, the referee decides what would have happened. Interference with the posts during a free or sideline puck leads to a retake.

rules.title: Own goal
rules.text: If a defender plays the ball through their own scoring space, the score counts for the attacking team.

rules.title: Overcarrying (too many steps)
rules.text: Technical foul: carrying the ball in the hand for more than four steps, or holding it for longer than four steps would take. Commonly called overcarrying or 'taking too many steps'. Penalty: free puck to the other team.

rules.title: Throwing the ball / illegal handpass
rules.text: Technical foul: throwing the ball, or handpassing it without a clear striking action of the hand. Commonly called 'a throw' or 'he threw it'. Penalty: free puck to the other team.

rules.title: Picking the ball off the ground
rules.text: Technical foul: touching the ball on the ground with the hand, unless the player has fallen or been knocked down. Commonly called 'picking it up'. Penalty: free puck to the other team.

rules.title: Taking the ball into the hand too often
rules.text: Technical foul: catching the ball or bringing it into the hand more than twice before playing it away. Penalty: free puck to the other team.

rules.title: Catching your own release
rules.text: Technical foul: dropping the ball from the hand and catching it again without striking it with the hurley. Penalty: free puck to the other team.

rules.title: Square ball (in the small rectangle too early)
rules.text: Technical foul: an attacking player is inside the small rectangle before the ball arrives, with some exceptions. Commonly called 'square ball'. Any score is disallowed and a free puck is awarded to the defending team.

rules.title: Carrying the ball over the goal-line
rules.text: Technical foul: an attacker carries the ball over the opponents' goal-line. Penalty: free puck to the defending team.

rules.title: Not retreating at a free or sideline
rules.text: Technical foul: opponents are closer than 20m to a free or 13m to a sideline before it is struck. Penalty: the free is moved 13m to a more advantageous position, up to the 20m line.

rules.title: Taker playing the ball twice
rules.text: Technical foul: the taker of a free or sideline plays the ball again before another player touches it, unless it rebounds off the posts or crossbar. Penalty: free puck to the other team.

rules.title: Lifting a sideline
rules.text: Technical foul: the taker of a sideline puck tries to lift the ball. A sideline must be struck off the ground. Penalty: free puck to the other team.

rules.title: Category I aggressive fouls
rules.text: Aggressive fouls such as pulling an opponent down, tripping, abusive language to an opponent, rough play, illegal pulling with the hurley, careless use of the hurley and throwing the hurley dangerously. Penalty: free puck from where it happened. The first offence is a caution (yellow card); a second cautionable offence is an order-off (red card).

rules.title: Feigning a foul or injury
rules.text: Aggressive foul: pretending to be fouled or injured (diving). Penalty: caution, then order-off for a second cautionable offence; free puck from where play stopped.

rules.title: Illegal charge
rules.text: Aggressive foul: charging an opponent from behind or in the front, or charging to give a teammate an advantage. Penalty: free puck; a caution for persistent fouling and an order-off if it continues.

rules.title: Pushing, holding the hurley and obstruction
rules.text: Aggressive fouls such as pushing, holding an opponent's hurley, charging the goalkeeper in the small rectangle, obstructing with the hurley, or striking an opponent's hurley illegally. Penalty: free puck; caution for persistent fouling, order-off if it continues.

rules.title: Category III aggressive fouls
rules.text: Striking or kicking an opponent with minimal force, dangerous behaviour such as grabbing a helmet or faceguard, spitting at an opponent, or joining a melee. Penalty: order-off (red card) and a free puck.

rules.title: Category IV aggressive fouls
rules.text: Striking, kicking or stamping on an opponent with force or causing injury through reckless play, or abusive language towards a match official. Penalty: order-off (red card) and a free puck.

rules.title: Fouls against match officials
rules.text: Threatening or abusive conduct, physical interference, or assault towards a referee or other match official. Penalty: order-off (red card) and a free puck.

rules.title: Fouling after a free is given
rules.text: If a player retaliates or fouls between a free being awarded and it being taken, the free is cancelled, the game restarts with a throw-in where the first foul happened, and any other penalties still apply.

rules.title: Advantage
rules.text: When a team is fouled, the referee may play advantage by raising an arm for up to five seconds. If no real advantage follows, the referee brings play back and awards a free from where the foul happened. A card can still be given afterwards.

rules.title: Denying a goalscoring chance (black card)
rules.text: In inter-county senior, under-20 and minor games only: if an attacker with a clear goalscoring chance is pulled down, tripped or fouled with the hurley, a penalty puck is awarded and the offender gets a black card and ten minutes in the sin bin. It does not apply to club games.

rules.title: Dissent: challenging the referee
rules.text: Challenging the authority of a match official. Penalty: caution (yellow card); order-off for a second cautionable offence.

rules.title: Dissent over a free
rules.text: If a player shows dissent about a free given against their team, the free is moved 30m more advantageous, up to the opponents' 20m line. This can only be applied once per incident; further dissent is dealt with under 6.1. At under-18 and younger grades, the offender also gets a black card and ten minutes in the sin bin.
rules.source: GAA referee guidance on new hurling rules, effective 28 March 2026

rules.title: Refusing to leave the field
rules.text: If a player refuses to leave the field when ordered off, or comes back on, the referee gives a three-minute warning and may end the game if the player still does not comply.
